news.title: Arsenal 2nd, Leeds 17th - the major omen looming over the 2026-27 season
news.lede: Manchester City and Arsenal are among the clubs that could suffer a World Cup hangover going into the 2026-27 season, if you assess the total number of minutes played. Leeds United, meanwhile, have done very well out of this summer’s tournament. Man City, Arsenal, Liverpool, Aston Villa and Crystal Palace are the five Premier League clubs whose players clocked up the most minutes at the 2026 World Cup, but the top two lead the way by a considerable margin. City’s players notched up 800 minutes more than Arsenal at the World Cup, a large part of that down to key midfielder Rodri, who played almost every minute of Spain’s triumphant World Cup win.

news.title: ‘Weekday games were amazing’: pubs toast extra £150m in World Cup sales
news.lede: England’s progress provides best football-related uplift of recent years, with one pub too packed to host its Dolly Parton tribute. Late opening hours and England’s progress to the semi-final of an expanded World Cup helped provide the best football-related uplift of recent years for pubs, figures suggest. Pubs poured 30m extra pints over the course of the tournament compared with a normal trading period, with busy pumps delivering £150m in added sales, according to the British Beer & Pubs Association (BBPA). The World Cup-related increase in sales, as fans followed England and Scotland games, also appears to have outstripped that seen during previous competitions, including England’s run to the final of Euro 2024.

news.title: How the death of Jayden Adams shook a community: ‘Being on the pitch was his happy place’
news.lede: Those who knew the South African, who died aged 25 not long after playing at the World Cup, describe a humble and hard-working man who cared about friends and family. For Jayden Adams, the South Africa midfielder who died this month at the age of 25, football was a “safe space”. Those words, used by Adams’s junior coach Steve Barker at his memorial service last Thursday, tell you everything you need to know about his life beyond the pitch. Adams’s battles were bestowed on him almost from birth.

news.title: FIFA letter to Argentina leaked amid World Cup final punishment decision
news.lede: FIFA president Gianni Infantino has come under scrutiny after a letter congratulating Argentina on their World Cup campaign emerged while the nation remains under investigation over the chaotic scenes that followed the final defeat to Spain. The letter, leaked by Argentine media, was sent to Argentine Football Association president Claudio Tapia after Lionel Scaloni's side finished runners-up at the 2026 World Cup. Its emergence comes at an awkward time for FIFA, with football's governing body still investigating the post-match melee involving several Argentina players and members of staff after their extra-time defeat in New Jersey. As is customary after every World Cup, Infantino wrote to the three medal-winning nations.

news.title: For the record: Our list of New Zealand’s 50 largest-ever football crowds
news.lede: If there’s one thing that’s defined the growing popularity of football in New Zealand, it’s the size of the crowds willing to pack our stadiums in recent years. Thanks in no small part to the 2023 FIFA Women’s World Cup, it’s becoming increasingly common for more than 20,000 to fill our grounds for international games and club games. In fact, more than half of the matches to draw crowds of more than 20,000 fans have taken place since mid-2023. The arrival of A-League club Auckland FC has provided capacity crowds at Go Media Stadium (formerly known as Mt Smart Stadium), and in July 2026 they set a record for a men’s game in New Zealand when 40,112 watched them play Tottenham Hotspur at Eden Park.

news.title: Haaland steals the show at Gianluigi Donnarumma’s wedding
news.lede: Remember the viral Viking Row celebration that became synonymous with Norway’s remarkable journey at the 2026 FIFA World Cup? Erling Haaland was at the heart of it, regularly leading the celebrations after Norway’s matches.This time, however, the Norwegian superstar recreated it as he stole the spotlight at Gianluigi Donnarumma’s wedding in Italy, leading guests in a spirited rendition of Norway’s famous Viking Row.. Donnarumma married his longtime partner Alessia Elefante in a lavish ceremony in Fasano, with a star-studded guest list that included Pep Guardiola, Paolo Maldini, Sandro Tonali and Nicolo Barella.The couple first met in 2016 in Castellammare di Stabia, their hometown near Naples. Elefante, an interior designer, and Donnarumma welcomed their son, Leo, in 2024.

news.title: Argentina could be stripped of four key players after World Cup final meltdown
news.lede: Argentina face a massive rebuilding job following their disgraceful conduct during and after the World Cup final. Argentina elevated their notorious tactics to unprecedented levels at the MetLife Stadium, employing ultra-defensive, cynical methods in a desperate attempt to take the game penalties. The strategy came close to succeeding until Spain finally penetrated the Argentine defence through Ferran Torres's extra-time winner. Regardless of whether you admire or despise their methods, the team's success has to be respected.

news.title: Bayern Munich among top five clubs to be compensated by FIFA following World Cup
news.lede: The relationship between club and international football has always been shaky at best. Clubs fear injuries that could derail an entire season while international teams pine for their nation’s top talents — a complex conflict of interest. Nowhere is the conflict as prominent as the FIFA World Cup. Clubs have no choice but to surrender their talent to their national teams.
